objective: Test a rule that reads the atoms, and so the genus, of every three-fold space from creation alone: twins first pick out the atoms' lines, then twins compared on those lines alone give the atoms. Run it on the census and on larger random spaces with plane glue, with exact creation maps, and state what is proved.
status: Proved: the two-stage twin rule reads every Fano tree whose atoms have at most four cuts; by exact computation it reads all 111 census spaces and 57 of 80 random spaces, and in 15 random glued spaces two lines of different atoms are twins of the yes/no creation relation, so no rule reading only whether creation occurs can return the atoms there; which far side creates separates every such pair
title: Reading the atoms through glue
